title: Free Is Not Open: Price and Permission

zones.label: Free and open
zones.summary: Free and open: costs nothing and grants permissions.
facts: Chapter 1 example: a lesson plan with a CC BY license.
The user pays nothing and may edit and share it, with credit to the author.
It passes both OER tests: an educational resource, under an open license.

zones.label: Open, with a paid print copy
zones.summary: Open, with a paid print copy: the license, not the price, makes it OER.
facts: Chapter 1 example: an open textbook that a print shop sells at cost.
The digital copy is free; the printed copy costs money.
The license still lets a campus print shop make copies without asking the publisher.
It is OER. "OER must cost nothing" is a common misunderstanding.

zones.label: Free but closed
zones.summary: Free but closed: no price, but no permission to edit or share.
facts: Chapter 1 example: a publisher's sample chapter marked "All rights reserved".
You may read it, but copyright's default of all rights reserved still applies.
It is not OER because it has no open license.

zones.label: Paid and closed
zones.summary: Paid and closed: costs money and grants no permissions.
facts: Chapter 1 example: a commercial textbook from the campus store.
The student pays and still may not edit or share it.
Many resources you meet in school sit in this zone.

quiz.question: Which zone holds a publisher's sample chapter marked "All rights reserved"?
quiz.explanation: It costs nothing, but all rights are reserved.

quiz.question: Which zone holds a lesson plan licensed CC BY 4.0 that costs the user nothing?
Which zone shows an open resource where only the printed copy costs money?
quiz.explanation: The license grants the permissions, so the paid print copy is still OER.

quiz.question: Which zone holds a commercial textbook from the campus store?
quiz.explanation: It costs money and grants no permissions.
